# Construction Intelligence Engine — Implementation Plan

Status: Proposed v0.1
Depends on: `docs/CONSTRUCTION_INTELLIGENCE_SPEC.md`
Reference project: 101 Meydenbauer, Building B

## 0. Delivery strategy

Build this as a sequence of **vertical proofs**, not horizontal infrastructure layers.

Each milestone must leave Meydenbauer more useful than before. Avoid a long rewrite in which the current bid model stops working while a generalized framework is constructed underneath it.

Governing migration rule:

> **Wrap -> prove -> extract -> generalize.**

The current takeoff, model, schedule, logistics and animation pipeline remains operational until its replacement has passed the same or stronger checks.

---

## 1. Success condition

The first release is successful when one project can move through this chain without separate sources of truth:

```text
source evidence
  -> normalized claims
  -> canonical project state
  -> scenario derivation
  -> geometry + quantities + activities + issues
  -> Blender / GLB / Explorer / report / film
```

The signature demonstration is the Meydenbauer depth question:

`POC depth change -> trench condition -> slab SF -> excavation -> logistics -> schedule implication -> visual decision`

If that chain is real, the architecture is real.

---

## 2. Workstream map

| Workstream | Outcome | Depends on |
|---|---|---|
| A. Semantic kernel | stable IDs + typed state + validation | none |
| B. Meydenbauer adapter | existing pipeline emits canonical state | A |
| C. Scenario graph | S1/S2/S3 and depth deltas propagate | A, B |

Workstreams overlap only after their contracts are stable enough to avoid churn.

# Meydenbauer Reference Acceptance

Status: Proposed v0.1
Purpose: Golden-reference acceptance contract for the Construction Intelligence Engine (CIE)

## 1. Why this exists

Architecture is cheap to describe. This document makes it expensive to fake.

CIE is accepted only when it can demonstrate construction reasoning end-to-end on the existing Meydenbauer under-slab re-pipe without weakening the checks already present in the project.

The tests below are product tests, not merely unit tests.

---

## 2. Reference facts to preserve

At the time this acceptance contract was written, the current Meydenbauer deliverables report:

- four ground-floor units: B-101 through B-104;
- approximately 312.75 LF of modeled new under-slab ABS;
- four POC cleanouts/tie-ins;
- approximately 105 LF of 2-inch, 33 LF of 3-inch and 175 LF of 4-inch pipe;
- S1 slab cut: 590 SF;
- S2 slab cut: 686 SF;
- S3 reference slab cut: 991 SF;
- allowance reference: 700 SF;
- S2 base excavation at the 3.5 ft POC-invert assumption: approximately 82.3 bank CY;
- 30 fixture/stack connections in the S2 pit assumption;
- B-104 is the largest unit by modeled pipe length and S2 slab area;
- the current strawman unit-by-unit sequence totals 81.5 working days before holidays and preconstruction;
- current unit order is B-103 -> B-102 -> B-101 -> B-104;
- the existing sequence build includes 92 unit-sequence checks and 44 framing checks.

These values are regression fixtures, not license to hard-code the result.

---

## 3. Acceptance A — Identity and evidence

### Test A1 — Select a modeled pipe

Given a known B-104 pipe element in the canonical state:

- it has a stable `cie_id`;
- Blender geometry carries that ID;
- exported GLB geometry can resolve that ID;
- Explorer selection resolves to exactly one canonical element.

**Pass:** all surfaces agree on identity.

### Test A2 — Trace to source

From the selected pipe, the user can navigate to its claim(s) and evidence locator(s), including the relevant P1.02 reference.

**Pass:** the source can be identified without searching README prose or source code.

### Test A3 — Separate plan and elevation confidence

The selected pipe can express different provenance states for plan position, size and elevation.

The owner selected **new supply routes installed alongside the existing system, followed by one-unit-at-a-time cutover**. This animation illustrates that strategy with the Unit 107 drawing study and its five-fixture bathroom pilot. It is a proposal for discussion, not a contractor-approved means-and-methods plan or a verified survey of installed piping.

## What moves

1. A representative floor-protection area appears at the bathroom pilot.
2. New distribution routes grow alongside the gray drawing reference.
3. Branches extend toward fixtures; nine pilot tie points remain disconnected.
4. The animation pauses at a testing/acceptance gate. It does not report a passed test.
5. During the scheduled cutover, nine ties switch in five fixture groups. The displayed unit boundary must be established in the field; this model does not prove independent unit isolation.
6. Service verification follows. Moving color markers indicate the sequence, not a flow or temperature simulation.
7. Only pilot terminal references fade. Shared mains stay visible because their other users are not established. The sequence then points to the next unit.

The illustration includes 37 concept routes reused from the Unit 107 domestic-water topology. Only the bathroom's nine fixture connections are explicit in the cutover demonstration. Other Unit 107 connections, shared building risers, plant interfaces and subsequent units need separate design and isolation planning. The animation is not evidence that those connections are resolved.

`repipe-strategy.json` is the sequencing specification, generated by `prepare.py`. It records the reference-spec hash, owner-selected strategy, phase timing, route IDs, nine fixture ports and every assumption. The drawing-reference model remains unchanged. The viewer places reference and proposed geometry in separate scene groups; it does not relabel the reference as a verified as-built.

Every proposed route, tie point and protection graphic is **assumed**. Reference topology is reused to explain the sequence, not selected as final replacement routing. New paths are separated by **0.25 m for graphical legibility only**, not a proposed construction offset or verified clearance. Nominal diameters are enlarged 1.5× with a minimum display radius of 10 mm. Pipe sizes, materials, fittings, isolation points, access openings, protection/staging/egress limits and shutdown duration remain to be established. There are no construction quantities, test-pressure prescriptions or promises of uninterrupted service.

P4.01 supplies the underlying Unit A/107 reference. A2.03 and A3.11 support the prior grid calibration and floor datums. The original plumbing PDF annotations identify systems, risers and a floor-protection annotation on another sheet; no documented repipe method was found in the reviewed annotations/model notes. ## Source and status

- [Installation specification](installation/highland-installation-proposed.yaml) governs the proposed geometry. Every new physical element is **assumed**; source drawings establish relationships, not measured installation dimensions.
- [Existing-reference specification](installation/highland-installation-existing-reference.yaml) remains separate. The user's report of failing CPVC does not establish surveyed existing routes.

# Highland lobby-to-corridor drone view

A 26-second, portrait flight for a phone: the camera approaches the east facade, crosses the broad glazed entrance of Lobby 110, follows its connector into Corridor 108, enters an illustrative elevator, rises to R2, and continues down Corridor 208 toward the stair. An interactive, self-contained HTML viewer has Play/Pause and scrubbing; the MP4 uses the same camera path and adds a synthesized stereo score. The walkthrough is a presentation study of public circulation, not an as-built interior survey.

## Basis

- `../exterior/exterior.spec.json` and its GLB establish the exterior footprint, R1 level and the east `east-R1-08` entry opening. This opening is classified **entry** in the model; A2.03 shows lobby glazing/doors there. The flight does not assert a separate operable window.
- Architectural sheets **A2.03 and A2.04**, dated 04-02-07, locate **Lobby 110**, **Corridors 108/208**, two elevators, and Stair M1. A2.03 labels the core corridor at **6 ft**. A3.11 supplies R1/R2 floor elevations 353.00/363.25 ft, a 10 ft 3 in rise. The PDF SHA-256 is in `flight.spec.json`; high-resolution crops are in `source-review/`.
- The lobby, connector and long corridor rectangles in `flight.spec.json` are manually fitted to the plans and rounded. They use the exterior study's plan-coordinate system in inches. The six-foot R1 width is documented; R2 reuse and exact wall faces are provisional. The path and test points are recorded in feet for readability.

The existing exterior GLB contains no real interior partitions. Floors, walls, ceiling (assumed 8 ft 6 in clear), doors, elevator cab/fronts, stair door, fixtures, lighting and finishes in this tour are **illustrative**. A short dark transition at the glazing covers the switch to the plan-based interior. The vertical rise is documented, while the elevator car and door timing are not. This model does not depict residential unit interiors, concealed plumbing or an egress survey. The entry doors open with camera proximity; the elevator doors use the presentation timing. The gold ribbon traces the camera route, not a construction or accessible route. Upper-floor window illumination, tree motion, the external glass/brass elevator section, and warm area lights are visual treatments. Nearby building footprints come from an OpenStreetMap Overpass snapshot (`osm-buildings-source.json`, © OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL 1.0); registration to the exterior model and most surrounding heights are approximate. The street trees are procedural presentation assets.

## Build and check

Requirements: Python 3 with NumPy and Pillow, Node, npm, Chromium and FFmpeg. The build installs pinned `three`, `esbuild` and `playwright` packages from `package-lock.json` when needed, and uses the published exterior GLB. The source PDF is needed only to re-evaluate the manual geometry picks, not to run the animation.

```bash

```

Headless rendering checks the entrance ID, building/interior mesh counts, camera positions at every phase, the one-floor rise, mobile overflow, playback and browser errors. Full rendering encodes 624 frames at 24 fps to a 720 x 1280 H.264 MP4 with `faststart` for phone playback; `audio.py` generates the stereo score and muxes AAC without re-encoding the video. The browser checks verify animation behavior, not the accuracy of undimensioned interior walls. The deliverable viewer embeds the GLB and scripts; it opens as one HTML file after download. The native Blender reconstruction now includes the interior, camera, doors, elevator and animated section; see [Blender instructions](BLENDER.md). It renders with Cycles CPU or a configured GPU.

The **Highland Blender preview** workflow (`.github/workflows/highland-blender-preview.yaml`) opens the existing exterior `.blend` with `bpy==5.0.1`, renders one 540 × 960 portrait PNG using Cycles on the GitHub-hosted CPU, and uploads the image plus a source/version manifest. ```

Use Python 3.11 with `bpy==5.0.1`; the system Blender 4.3 cannot open this Blender 5 file. This preview workflow renders the exterior only. The complete native interior and animation are built by `build_blender.py`; the separate **Highland native Blender film** workflow renders and assembles the full flight. See [Blender instructions](BLENDER.md). A standard GitHub-hosted runner provides no OptiX GPU; budget a CPU preview before deciding whether to use a self-hosted GPU runner for a full film.

The prior exterior study has unresolved facade/window differences. This flight relies on the R1 east lobby entry and the public-hall labels and does not resolve those exterior differences. # Model from drawings or photos

Follow `docs/METHOD.md` (rules) and `docs/RUNBOOK.md` (exact commands). This is the order and the gates.

## 0. Orient
```bash
uv run bm doctor          # need: bpy for builds; sources present for intake
uv run bm list --json     # does the site already exist? which specs?
```
If bpy is missing locally, you can still write and validate specs (`bm check`), and CI builds them.

## 1. Site
New jobsite: `uv run bm new <site> --type element|detail --name "<display name>"`, then fill
`projects/<site>/project.yaml` (address, building type, scope). Put source PDFs/photos in
`projects/<site>/sources/` (never committed) and inventory each one in `sources/manifest.json`
(file, sha256, sheet ids, revision/date, scale, photo ids).

## 2. Pick the model type
- **detail**: one section (rake, eave, balcony edge, window head) → start from `templates/project/specs/detail.yaml`;
  example `projects/qp-cottage-a/specs/qp-rake-ah700-12.yaml`.
- **house**: plan-extracted shell + takeoff → RUNBOOK steps 2–11; example `projects/qp-cottage-a/specs/qp-cottage-a.yaml`.
- **element**: boxes per member (framing bay, deck) → `templates/project/specs/element.yaml`.
- **room**: photo-only interior → `projects/room-living-kitchen/specs/room-living-kitchen.yaml`.
- Existing condition and proposed repair → two specs (`<x>-existing.yaml`, `<x>-proposed.yaml`).

## 3. Takeoff into the spec (gates)
- Calibrate each sheet from its own dimension strings (`uv run bm calibrate scale …`); never trust the title block.
- Every element: `confirmed` + `source` (dimension on a document), `provisional` + `source` + how measured and
  tolerance, or `assumed` + `basis`. Actual lumber sizes. Never scale an NTS detail.
- Add document-driven `checks` (counts, overall extents, gaps, elevations) each with a `source`.
- Conflicting sources: model the governing one, write the conflict into `flags:`.

## 4. Build and verify
```bash
uv run bm check --no-tests                     # provenance errors without bpy
uv run bm build <site>/<spec> --no-render       # checks only, seconds
uv run bm build <site>/<spec>                   # + review renders in build/<site>/<spec>/
```
Read `build/<site>/<spec>/report.md`, then **look at** the review PNGs (plan/front/side/iso, provenance
colors). Where an elevation exists: `uv run bm overlay …` (RUNBOOK step 10) and report the edge agreement.
No local bpy: push a branch and read the `build-models` run instead.

## 5. Report back
State: checks passed (n/n), renders looked at (which), overlays (agreement %), every assumed element, and
what is not modeled. Never call provisional or assumed geometry documented.

    names = list(pixels)

        "distance_in": [distances[name] for name in names],

"""Extract sheet registration and riser markups from the governing plumbing set.

Needs the source PDF in projects/highland/sources/ (git-ignored). Writes the committed
source-review/plan-marks.json and review crops; takeoff.py reads only the JSON, so CI never
needs the PDF.

Registration: the grid bubbles on every P2.0x sheet are found with a Hough circle search and
fitted to the A2.03 grid dimension strings by least squares (no title-block scale is used).
Markups: the drawings carry vector PDF annotations (Square = riser box, colored by the sheet
legend: green "continuous riser or riser going up", orange "riser going down"). Their
rectangles are transformed through the page rotation into grid inches.
"""
import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
import pymupdf

from bmodels.paths import PROJECTS

SITE = PROJECTS / "highland"
HERE = Path(__file__).parent
PDF = SITE / "sources" / "RL- REVISED Highland Condos Plumbing 10-29-07.pdf"
OUT = HERE / "source-review"

# A2.03 (full set page 47, 04-02-07): grid dimension strings, inches. X east from grid 7,
# Y north from grid E. 6-7 16'-3", 7-8 27'-9", 8-9 27'-9", 9-10 31'-3" (top string);
# A-B 30'-6", B-C 27'-0", C-D 17'-6", D-E 17'-6", E-F 18'-0", F-G 24'-6", G-H 15'-0" (right string).
GRID_X = {"6": -195, "7": 0, "8": 333, "9": 666, "10": 1041}
GRID_Y = {"A": 1110, "B": 744, "C": 420, "D": 210, "E": 0, "F": -216, "G": -510, "H": -690}
SHEETS = {4: ("P2.01", "P2"), 5: ("P2.02", "P1"), 6: ("P2.03", "R1"), 7: ("P2.04", "R2"),
          8: ("P2.05", "R3"), 9: ("P2.06", "R4"), 10: ("P2.07", "R5")}
LEGEND = {(0.0, 1.0, 0.5): "UP", (1.0, 0.5, 0.0): "DN"}
PLAN_MIN_X_PT = 1300  # markups left of this are the sheet legend, not plan marks


def bubbles(page):
    import cv2
    z = 2.0
    pix = page.get_pixmap(matrix=pymupdf.Matrix(z, z), colorspace=pymupdf.csGRAY)
    im = np.frombuffer(pix.samples, np.uint8).reshape(pix.height, pix.width)
    found = {}
    for strip, (x0, y0, x1, y1) in {"top": (1300, 80, 2450, 160), "right": (2600, 320, 2690, 1780)}.items():
        crop = im[int(y0 * z):int(y1 * z), int(x0 * z):int(x1 * z)]
        c = cv2.HoughCircles(cv2.GaussianBlur(crop, (5, 5), 1), cv2.HOUGH_GRADIENT, 1, 60,
                             param1=120, param2=30, minRadius=22, maxRadius=32)
        found[strip] = [] if c is None else [(x / z + x0, y / z + y0) for x, y, _ in c[0]]
    xs = sorted(p[0] for p in found["top"])
    ys = sorted(p[1] for p in found["right"])
    assert len(xs) == len(GRID_X) and len(ys) == len(GRID_Y), (len(xs), len(ys))
    return dict(zip(GRID_X, xs)), dict(zip(GRID_Y, ys))


def fit(pts, dist):
    a = np.array([[pts[k], 1] for k in dist]); v = np.array(list(dist.values()))
    (s, o), *_ = np.linalg.lstsq(a, v, rcond=None)
    return float(s), float(o), float(np.abs(a @ [s, o] - v).max())


def main():
    if not PDF.exists():
        sys.exit(f"missing {PDF.relative_to(SITE)}: restore it with `bm run highland/installation restore` "
                 "(Highland-original.pdf, sha256 93c5426c...) and copy it under that name")
    doc = pymupdf.open(PDF)
    OUT.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    result = {"source": PDF.name, "sha256_expected": "93c5426cc8604ec33abd0b13ece1f5c6b76fe0417a2efcd9aca84701d294586a",
              "units": "inches; x east of grid 7, y north of grid E",
              "grid_source": "A2.03 Level R1 plan, full set page 47, 04-02-07, grid dimension strings",
              "sheets": {}}
    for page_no, (sheet, level) in SHEETS.items():
        page = doc[page_no - 1]
        bx, by = bubbles(page)
        sx, ox, rx = fit(bx, GRID_X)
        sy, oy, ry = fit(by, GRID_Y)
        to_in = lambda p: [round(sx * p.x + ox, 1), round(sy * p.y + oy, 1)]  # noqa: E731
        boxes = []
        for a in page.annots():
            if a.type[1] != "Square":
                continue
            kind = LEGEND.get(tuple(round(c, 2) for c in (a.colors.get("stroke") or ())))
            r = a.rect * page.rotation_matrix
            if kind is None or r.x0 < PLAN_MIN_X_PT:
                continue
            boxes.append({"kind": kind, "center_in": to_in((r.tl + r.br) / 2),
                          "size_in": [round(abs(r.width * sx)), round(abs(r.height * sy))]})
        boxes.sort(key=lambda b: (-b["center_in"][1], b["center_in"][0]))
        result["sheets"][sheet] = {"page": page_no, "level": level,
                                   "pt_per_in": [round(1 / sx, 5), round(-1 / sy, 5)],
                                   "grid_residual_in": round(max(rx, ry), 2), "riser_boxes": boxes}
        print(sheet, level, "residual", round(max(rx, ry), 2), "in;", len(boxes), "riser boxes")
    (OUT / "plan-marks.json").write_text(json.dumps(result, indent=1) + "\n")
    crops(doc)


def crops(doc):
    """Review crops at each traced stack, R1-R5, so the takeoff can be checked without the PDF."""
    from PIL import Image, ImageDraw
    from takeoff import STACKS  # noqa: E402  (same folder)
    marks = json.loads((OUT / "plan-marks.json").read_text())
    for sid, st in STACKS.items():
        tiles = []
        for sheet, info in marks["sheets"].items():
            if info["level"] not in ("R1", "R2", "R3", "R4", "R5"):
                continue
            page = doc[info["page"] - 1]
            ptx, pty = info["pt_per_in"]
            x, y = st["xy_by_level"].get(info["level"], st["xy"])
            ox, oy = 1551.2, 1214.2  # grid 7 / E on the sheet frame (identical on P2.01-P2.07)
            r = pymupdf.Rect(ox + ptx * (x - 90), oy - pty * (y + 70), ox + ptx * (x + 90), oy - pty * (y - 70))
            pix = page.get_pixmap(dpi=150, clip=r)
            im = Image.frombytes("RGB", (pix.width, pix.height), pix.samples)
            ImageDraw.Draw(im).text((6, 4), f"{sheet} {info['level']}", fill=(200, 0, 0))
            tiles.append(im)
        w, h = tiles[0].size
        sheet_im = Image.new("RGB", (w * len(tiles), h), "white")
        for i, t in enumerate(tiles):
            sheet_im.paste(t, (i * w, 0))
        sheet_im.save(OUT / f"stack-{sid}.jpg", quality=80)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.path.insert(0, str(HERE))
    main()

"""Highland domestic-water risers and mains: takeoff -> existing and proposed specs (no bpy, no PDF).

Reads source-review/plan-marks.json (written by extract.py from the governing plumbing set) and the
picks below; writes risers-existing.spec.json and risers-proposed.spec.json. `--check` is the CI
step: regenerate both and let `git diff --exit-code` catch drift.

Coordinates: inches, x east of grid 7, y north of grid E, z above the P1 floor (342.00 ft).
Element status is the weakest of its plan position, elevation and size statuses.
"""
import json
import math
import sys
from pathlib import Path

HERE = Path(__file__).parent
MARKS = json.loads((HERE / "source-review" / "plan-marks.json").read_text())
RANK = {"confirmed": 2, "provisional": 1, "assumed": 0}

# --- documented datums ----------------------------------------------------------------------
LEVELS_FT = {"P2": 332.0, "P1": 342.0, "R1": 353.0, "R2": 363.25, "R3": 373.5, "R4": 383.75, "R5": 394.25}
DATUM_SRC = "A3.11 building sections 01/02, 04-02-07 (labeled floor elevations)"
Z0_FT = LEVELS_FT["P1"]
FLOORS = ["R1", "R2", "R3", "R4", "R5"]

# --- assumptions (no drawing gives domestic-water pipe elevations) --------------------------
CEILING_TAKEOFF_IN = 108   # branch groups at floor + 9 ft, i.e. above an assumed 8'-6" ceiling
MAIN_ELEV_FT = 350.5       # P1 garage main, hung below the R1 slab
TRIPLE_SPACING_IN = 4.0    # CW / HW / HWC centre-to-centre in a stack or header
BRANCH_STUB_IN = 24.0
ASSUMPTIONS = [
    {"id": "ceiling_takeoff_in", "basis": f"Floor + {CEILING_TAKEOFF_IN} in. P3.02 draws each branch group at the "
     "ceiling of the floor it serves; the Unit 107 study (highland/water) holds overhead CW at floor + 108 in. "
     "No document gives riser takeoff heights."},
    {"id": "main_elev_ft", "basis": f"{MAIN_ELEV_FT} ft. P1 garage main hung below the R1 slab; S3.8 gives the "
     "drop-slab soffit at 351.21 ft near Unit 107. The garage soffit along the main is not established."},
    {"id": "triple_spacing_in", "basis": f"{TRIPLE_SPACING_IN} in c/c. Riser symbols are not drawn to scale."},
    {"id": "branch_stub_in", "basis": f"{BRANCH_STUB_IN} in. Branches continue per the typical unit plans "
     "(P4.0x), which this model does not trace. Stub direction points away from Corridor 108."},
    {"id": "existing_material", "basis": "CPVC, per the owner's report of failing CPVC (highland/installation). "
     "P0.01 material notes were not used; installed material is not field verified."},
]

# --- traced picks ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Stack seeds: the riser box nearest each seed (within 40 in) on every listed level is averaged.
# Group mapping to P3.02's 01-05 is by floor count only (see flags).
STACKS = {
    "A": {"seed": (559, 804), "levels": ["R1", "R2", "R3"], "offset_at": "R4", "to_seed": (555, 747), "top": "R5"},
    "B": {"seed": (782, 761), "levels": ["R1", "R2", "R3", "R4", "R5"], "top": "R5"},
    "C": {"seed": (682, 358), "levels": ["R1", "R2", "R3"], "offset_at": "R4", "to_seed": (680, 475), "top": "R5"},
    "E": {"seed": (812, -113), "levels": ["R1", "R2", "R3"], "offset_at": "R4", "to_seed": (789, 193), "top": "R5"},
    "F": {"seed": (595, -230), "levels": ["R1", "R2", "R3", "R4"], "top": "R4", "profile": "03"},
    "D": {"seed": (679, 280), "levels": ["R1", "R2", "R3", "R4", "R5"], "top": "R5", "hose_bibb": True},
}
TRACE_TOL_IN = 12  # riser box centre vs riser symbol, plus raster picking
# Header and main routes traced from P2.03 / P2.02 linework (0.87 and 1.07 in per review pixel).
HEADER_X = 735
MAIN_RISER = (641, 819)
PLANT_TIE = (-32, 915)
MAIN_Y = 915
ROUTE_TOL_IN = 18
DROP_106_107 = (661, -113)

# Sizes (nominal in) by riser segment, ceiling to ceiling. P3.02 riser diagram is NTS: sizes only.
P302 = "P3.02 domestic water riser diagram, PDF page 13, 10-29-07"
PROFILES = {
    "typical": [  # 01/02/04/05: groups at R1..R5 ceilings
        ("R1", "R2", (2, 2, 0.75), "confirmed", P302 + ': "2"CW, HW & 3/4"HWC" at the header connection'),
        ("R2", "R3", (2, 2, 0.75), "provisional", P302 + ": unlabeled; continues the size below"),
        ("R3", "R4", (2, 1.5, 0.75), "confirmed", P302 + ': "2"CW, 1-1/2"HW & 3/4"HWC"'),
        ("R4", "R5", (1, 1, 0.5), "confirmed", P302 + ' "1"CW, HW & 1/2"HWC"; P2.06 R4 label at stack A'),
    ],
    "03": [  # one floor shorter: groups at R1..R4 ceilings
        ("R1", "R2", (2, 2, 0.75), "confirmed", P302 + ': "2"CW, HW & 3/4"HWC" ("03 stack)'),
        ("R2", "R3", (2, 1.5, 0.75), "confirmed", P302 + ': "2"CW, 1-1/2"HW & 3/4"HWC" ("03 stack)'),
        ("R3", "R4", (1, 1, 0.5), "confirmed", P302 + ': "1"CW, HW & 1/2"HWC" ("03 stack)'),
    ],
}
SYSTEMS = ("CW", "HW", "HWC")
HEADER_SIZE = ((3, 3, 1.25), "confirmed", P302 + ' "3"CW, HW & 1-1/4"HWC"; P2.03 Corridor 108 label (same)')
MAIN_SIZE = ((4, 3, 1.5), "confirmed", P302 + ' "4"CW, 3"HW & 1-1/2"HWC"; P2.02 and P2.03 riser labels (same)')
DROP_SIZE = ((1.5, 1.5, 0.75), "confirmed", 'P2.03 R1 riser label "1-1/2"CW, 1-1/2"HW & 3/4"HWC DN" (conflicts with P3.02)')

FLAGS = [
    {"topic": "Units 106/107 drop HW size", "modeled_per": "P2.03",
     "sources": ["P2.03 R1 plan: 1-1/2 in HW", "P3.02 riser diagram: 1-1/4 in HW"],
     "note": "Same issue (10-29-07). Modeled per the plan label at the riser; the engineer should confirm."},
    {"topic": "P3.02 stack numbers vs plan locations", "modeled_per": "P2.03-P2.07",
     "sources": ["P3.02 riser diagram (NTS)", "P2.03-P2.07 riser markups"],
     "note": "Plan stacks are named A-F by location. F is matched to P3.02 '03' because both stop one floor "
             "short of R5. A, B, C and E are not matched to 01, 02, 04 and 05."},
    {"topic": "04 stack R1 branch", "modeled_per": "P3.02",
     "sources": ["P3.02: 04 stack has four branch groups", "highland/water spec: R1 continuation unresolved"],
     "note": "This model gives A, B, C and E an R1 branch each (20 groups). P3.02 implies 19: one of the four "
             "has no R1 branch, and which one is unresolved."},
]


def z_ft(ft):
    return round((ft - Z0_FT) * 12, 2)


def ceil_z(level):
    return z_ft(LEVELS_FT[level]) + CEILING_TAKEOFF_IN


def sheet_for(level):
    return next((s, v) for s, v in MARKS["sheets"].items() if v["level"] == level)


def locate(seed, level):
    sheet, info = sheet_for(level)
    near = [b for b in info["riser_boxes"] if math.dist(b["center_in"], seed) <= 40]
    if not near:
        return None
    b = min(near, key=lambda b: math.dist(b["center_in"], seed))
    return {"sheet": sheet, "kind": b["kind"], "xy": b["center_in"], "size_in": b["size_in"]}


def stack_xy(seed, levels):
    hits = [h for lv in levels if (h := locate(seed, lv))]
    assert hits, seed
    x = sum(h["xy"][0] for h in hits) / len(hits); y = sum(h["xy"][1] for h in hits) / len(hits)
    spread = max(math.dist(h["xy"], (x, y)) for h in hits)
    return (round(x, 1), round(y, 1)), hits, round(spread, 1)


def worst(*s):
    return min(s, key=RANK.get)


class Spec:
    def __init__(self, scene):
        self.scene, self.elements = scene, []

    def add(self, **e):
        e.setdefault("scene", self.scene)
        st = [e[k] for k in ("xy_status", "z_status", "size_status") if k in e]
        e["status"] = worst(*st) if st else e["status"]
        if e["status"] != "confirmed":
            assert e.get("source") or e.get("basis"), e["id"]
        self.elements.append(e)
        return e


def lateral(direction, i, n=3, s=TRIPLE_SPACING_IN):
    """Offset of pipe i of n, perpendicular to a horizontal run direction ('x' or 'y')."""
    d = (i - (n - 1) / 2) * s
    return (0, d) if direction == "x" else (d, 0)


def build_existing():
    sp = Spec("existing")
    stacks = {}
    hdr_z = ceil_z("R1")
    main_z = z_ft(MAIN_ELEV_FT)
    zb = {"z_status": "assumed", "z_basis": "assumptions: ceiling_takeoff_in", "datum_source": DATUM_SRC}
    route = {"xy_status": "provisional", "xy_source": "P2.03 R1 plan linework, Corridor 108",
             "xy_tolerance_in": ROUTE_TOL_IN}

    def run(id_, system, pts, size, size_status, size_source, role, xy=None, z=None, terminal=False):
        return sp.add(id=id_, kind="pipe", system=system, role=role, points=[list(map(float, p)) for p in pts],
                      nominal_in=size, size_status=size_status, size_source=size_source,
                      material="CPVC", material_status="assumed", terminal=terminal, **(xy or route), **(z or zb))

    # P1 garage main: plant tie -> east -> riser to the R1 header.

    mz = {"z_status": "assumed", "z_basis": "assumptions: main_elev_ft", "datum_source": DATUM_SRC}
    mxy = {"xy_status": "provisional", "xy_source": "P2.02 P1 plan linework (garage) and riser box at the main",
           "xy_tolerance_in": ROUTE_TOL_IN}
    for i, s in enumerate(SYSTEMS):
        dx, dy = lateral("x", i)

"""Build the Highland riser specs in Blender: .blend, .glb, provenance review renders, report.

  python build.py [--spec existing|proposed|both] [--no-render] [--samples N]

Reads only the committed *.spec.json (written by takeoff.py). One object per spec element, with
cie-style custom properties (id, status, system, role) so the GLB can be inspected. Review renders
color by provenance status; pipes are drawn at 2x outside diameter for legibility only.
"""
import argparse
import json
import math
import os
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import bmesh
import bpy
from mathutils import Matrix, Vector

from bmodels.paths import BUILD
from bmodels.record import record_md, conflicts_md, review_md, assumptions_md, stamp_render
from bmodels.spec import STATUS_COLORS

HERE = Path(__file__).parent
OUT = Path(os.environ.get("BM_BUILD") or BUILD / "highland" / "risers")
IN = 0.0254
DISPLAY_OD_MULT = 2.0
SYSTEM_COLORS = {"CW": (0.10, 0.35, 0.85, 1), "HW": (0.85, 0.12, 0.10, 1), "HWC": (0.95, 0.55, 0.05, 1)}
FOOTPRINT_IN = (-195, -690, 1041, 1110)  # grid 6..10 x H..A; context only (assumed simplification)


def reset():
    bpy.ops.wm.read_factory_settings(use_empty=True)
    sc = bpy.context.scene
    sc.unit_settings.system = "IMPERIAL"
    sc.render.engine = "CYCLES"
    sc.cycles.device = "CPU"
    sc.view_settings.view_transform = "Standard"
    world = bpy.data.worlds.new("world"); sc.world = world
    world.use_nodes = True
    world.node_tree.nodes["Background"].inputs[0].default_value = (0.93, 0.94, 0.96, 1)
    world.node_tree.nodes["Background"].inputs[1].default_value = 0.9


_mats = {}


def mat(name, rgba, alpha=1.0):
    key = (name, alpha)
    if key in _mats:
        return _mats[key]
    m = bpy.data.materials.new(name); m.use_nodes = True
    b = m.node_tree.nodes["Principled BSDF"]
    b.inputs["Base Color"].default_value = rgba
    b.inputs["Roughness"].default_value = 0.55
    if alpha < 1:
        b.inputs["Alpha"].default_value = alpha
    m.diffuse_color = rgba
    _mats[key] = m
    return m


def v(p):
    return Vector((p[0] * IN, p[1] * IN, p[2] * IN))


def add_cyl(bm, a, b, r, seg=12):
    a, b = Vector(a), Vector(b); d = b - a
    if d.length < 1e-6:
        return
    geom = bmesh.ops.create_cone(bm, cap_ends=True, segments=seg, radius1=r, radius2=r, depth=d.length)
    rot = d.normalized().to_track_quat("Z", "Y").to_matrix().to_4x4()
    bmesh.ops.transform(bm, matrix=Matrix.Translation((a + b) / 2) @ rot, verts=geom["verts"])


def add_sphere(bm, c, r):
    geom = bmesh.ops.create_uvsphere(bm, u_segments=12, v_segments=8, radius=r)
    bmesh.ops.translate(bm, vec=Vector(c), verts=geom["verts"])


def add_box(bm, c, size):
    geom = bmesh.ops.create_cube(bm, size=1)
    bmesh.ops.scale(bm, vec=Vector(size), verts=geom["verts"])
    bmesh.ops.translate(bm, vec=Vector(c), verts=geom["verts"])


def obj_from(bm, name, material, coll, props):
    me = bpy.data.meshes.new(name); bm.to_mesh(me); bm.free()
    ob = bpy.data.objects.new(name, me); coll.objects.link(ob)
    me.materials.append(material)
    for k, val in props.items():
        if val is not None:
            ob[k] = val if isinstance(val, (int, float, str)) else json.dumps(val)
    return ob


def element_mesh(e, mult):
    bm = bmesh.new()
    k = e["kind"]
    if k == "pipe":
        r = (e["nominal_in"] + 0.125) / 2 * IN * mult
        pts = [v(p) for p in e["points"]]
        for a, b in zip(pts, pts[1:]):
            add_cyl(bm, a, b, r)
        for p in pts[1:-1]:
            add_sphere(bm, p, r * 1.15)
    elif k in ("valve", "tie"):
        s = (e.get("nominal_in", 1) + 1.5) * IN * (1.4 if k == "valve" else 1.0)
        (add_box(bm, v(e["at"]), (s, s, s * 1.3)) if k == "valve" else add_sphere(bm, v(e["at"]), s * 0.7))
    elif k in ("penetration", "firestop", "clamp"):
        r = e.get("radius_in", 6) * IN * (1.0 if k != "clamp" else 0.7)
        c = v(e["at"]); h = (8 if k == "penetration" else 2) * IN
        add_cyl(bm, c - Vector((0, 0, h / 2)), c + Vector((0, 0, h / 2)), r, seg=20)
    elif k == "opening":
        if "points" in e:  # ceiling strip
            a, b = v(e["points"][0]), v(e["points"][1]); d = b - a
            n = Vector((-d.y, d.x, 0)).normalized() * e["width_in"] * IN / 2
            verts = [bm.verts.new(p) for p in (a - n, b - n, b + n, a + n)]
        else:      # chase face, vertical
            c = v(e["at"]); w = e["width_in"] * IN / 2; h = e["height_in"] * IN
            verts = [bm.verts.new(c + Vector(o)) for o in ((-w, 0, 0), (w, 0, 0), (w, 0, h), (-w, 0, h))]
        bm.faces.new(verts)
    elif k == "note":
        return None
    return bm


def build_scene(spec, label, mode, mult):
    coll = bpy.data.collections.new(label); bpy.context.scene.collection.children.link(coll)
    ctx = bpy.data.collections.new(label + "-context"); bpy.context.scene.collection.children.link(ctx)
    x0, y0, x1, y1 = FOOTPRINT_IN
    slab = mat("context-slab", (0.75, 0.76, 0.78, 1), alpha=0.18)
    for lv, ft in spec["levels_ft"].items():
        if lv in ("P2",):
            continue
        z = (ft - 342.0) * 12
        bm = bmesh.new(); add_box(bm, v(((x0 + x1) / 2, (y0 + y1) / 2, z - 4)), ((x1 - x0) * IN, (y1 - y0) * IN, 8 * IN))
        ob = obj_from(bm, f"slab-{lv}", slab, ctx, {"cie_type": "context", "cie_status": "assumed",
                                                    "basis": "grid-extent box at the A3.11 floor elevation; not the slab outline"})
        ob.display_type = "WIRE" if mode == "review" else "SOLID"
        slab.blend_method = "BLEND" if hasattr(slab, "blend_method") else None
    counts = {}
    for e in spec["elements"]:
        bm = element_mesh(e, mult)
        if bm is None:
            continue
        counts[e["status"]] = counts.get(e["status"], 0) + 1
        if mode == "review":
            m = mat("status-" + e["status"], STATUS_COLORS[e["status"]], alpha=0.5 if e["kind"] == "opening" else 1)
        else:
            m = mat("sys-" + e.get("system", "x"), SYSTEM_COLORS.get(e.get("system"), (0.6, 0.6, 0.6, 1)),
                    alpha=0.5 if e["kind"] == "opening" else 1)
        obj_from(bm, e["id"], m, coll, {"cie_id": e["id"], "cie_type": e["kind"], "cie_status": e["status"],
                                        "cie_system": e.get("system"), "role": e.get("role"), "material": e.get("material"),
                                        "nominal_in": e.get("nominal_in"), "phase": e.get("phase"),
                                        "source": e.get("source"), "basis": e.get("basis")})
    return coll, counts


def camera(name, loc, rot_deg, ortho=None, lens=35):
    cam = bpy.data.cameras.new(name)
    if ortho:
        cam.type = "ORTHO"; cam.ortho_scale = ortho
    else:
        cam.lens = lens
    ob = bpy.data.objects.new(name, cam); bpy.context.scene.collection.objects.link(ob)
    ob.location = loc; ob.rotation_euler = [math.radians(a) for a in rot_deg]
    return ob


def lights():
    sun = bpy.data.lights.new("sun", "SUN"); sun.energy = 3.0
    ob = bpy.data.objects.new("sun", sun); bpy.context.scene.collection.objects.link(ob)
    ob.rotation_euler = (math.radians(50), math.radians(10), math.radians(35))


def render_views(name, spec, counts, samples):
    sc = bpy.context.scene
    sc.cycles.samples = samples
    sc.render.resolution_x, sc.render.resolution_y = 1600, 1000
    cx, cy = 470 * IN, 300 * IN
    views = {
        "iso": camera("cam-iso", (cx + 55, cy - 60, 50), (60, 0, 40), lens=30),
        "plan": camera("cam-plan", (cx, cy, 80), (0, 0, 0), ortho=52),
        "south": camera("cam-south", (cx, cy - 80, 5.5), (90, 0, 0), ortho=26),
        "east": camera("cam-east", (cx + 80, cy, 5.5), (90, 0, 90), ortho=26),
    }
    paths = []
    for vname, cam in views.items():
        sc.camera = cam
        path = OUT / f"{name}-{vname}.png"
        sc.render.filepath = str(path)
        bpy.ops.render.render(write_still=True)
        from PIL import Image, ImageStat
        st = ImageStat.Stat(Image.open(path).convert("L"))
        assert st.stddev[0] > 3, f"blank render {path}"
        stamp_render(path, spec, counts)
        paths.append(path.name)
    return paths


def report(name, spec, counts, renders):
    res = spec.get("checks", [])
    ok = all(c["pass"] for c in res)
    md = [f"# {spec['project']}", "",
          f"**{'PASS' if ok else 'FAIL'}** — {sum(c['pass'] for c in res)}/{len(res)} checks" if res else
          "No document checks on this spec (proposed; see the existing spec).",
          *record_md(spec), "", "## Provenance",
          *[f"- {k}: {counts.get(k, 0)}" for k in ("confirmed", "provisional", "assumed")],
          "", "## Checks", *[f"- {'PASS' if c['pass'] else 'FAIL'} {c['check']}: expected {c['expected']}, "
                             f"got {c['actual']} ({c['source']})" for c in res],
          *conflicts_md(spec, []), "", "## Assumptions", *assumptions_md(spec), *review_md(spec),
          "", "## Renders", *[f"- `{r}`" for r in renders],
          "", f"Pipes in review renders are drawn at {DISPLAY_OD_MULT}x outside diameter for legibility."]
    (OUT / f"{name}-report.md").write_text("\n".join(md) + "\n")
    (OUT / f"{name}-report.json").write_text(json.dumps({"spec": name, "pass": ok, "checks": res, "counts": counts,
                                                          "renders": renders}, indent=1) + "\n")
    return ok


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--spec", default="both", choices=["existing", "proposed", "both"])
    ap.add_argument("--no-render", action="store_true")
    ap.add_argument("--samples", type=int, default=16)
    a = ap.parse_args(sys.argv[sys.argv.index("--") + 1:] if "--" in sys.argv else sys.argv[1:])
    OUT.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    ok = True
    for name in (["existing", "proposed"] if a.spec == "both" else [a.spec]):
        spec = json.loads((HERE / f"risers-{name}.spec.json").read_text())
        reset(); lights()
        coll, counts = build_scene(spec, name, "review", DISPLAY_OD_MULT)
        renders = [] if a.no_render else render_views(name, spec, counts, a.samples)
        ok &= report(name, spec, counts, renders)
        # deliverable geometry at true outside diameter, colored by system
        reset(); lights()
        build_scene(spec, name, "system", 1.0)
        bpy.ops.wm.save_as_mainfile(filepath=str(OUT / f"highland-risers-{name}.blend"), compress=True)
        bpy.ops.export_scene.gltf(filepath=str(OUT / f"highland-risers-{name}.glb"), export_extras=True,
                                  export_apply=True)
        print(name, counts, "renders:", renders)
    sys.exit(0 if ok else 1)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

# Highland domestic-water risers and mains

**What it produces:** two separate models of the building's domestic water distribution, from the P1 garage
main through the R1 Corridor 108 header to every riser and floor takeoff up to R5:

- **existing** (`risers-existing.spec.json`): the system as drawn in the October 2007 plumbing set;
- **proposed** (`risers-proposed.spec.json`): a PEX-A replacement installed alongside the live system, then cut
  over one stack at a time. Every proposed element is **assumed**, and none of it is engineered.

Each spec builds to a `.blend`, a `.glb` (with `cie_id`, `cie_status`, `cie_system`, `phase` on every object) and
four labelled review renders. Deliverables: [../../deliverables/risers](../../deliverables/risers/README.md).

**Illustrative, not a contract document.** Drawing-traced, not a survey of installed piping.

## Sources

Registered in [source-manifest.json](source-manifest.json). The PDFs stay in `projects/highland/sources/`.

| Document | Used for | Status in the model |
|---|---|---|
| RL-REVISED Highland Condos Plumbing 10-29-07, P2.01–P2.07 | Riser positions (vector markups), main and header routes (linework) | XY **provisional**, ±12 in at risers, ±18 in on runs |
| same set, P3.02 riser diagram (NTS) | Stack topology, branch groups, pipe sizes | sizes **confirmed** where labelled; never scaled |
| A2.03 (04-02-07) grid dimension strings | Registration of every P2.0x sheet | grid **confirmed**; fit residual ≤ 0.28 in |
| A3.11 (04-02-07) | Floor elevations P1 342.00 … R5 394.25 ft | datums **confirmed** |
| S3.8 (04-02-07) | R1 drop-slab soffit 351.21 ft (bounds the garage main) | reference only |

How the trace works:

- The plumbing sheets carry vector PDF markups that follow the sheet legend: green "continuous riser or riser
  going up", orange "riser going down", and cyan, magenta and lime for CW, HW and HWC.
- `extract.py` finds the grid bubbles on each sheet and fits them to the A2.03 dimension strings. Every P2.0x
  sheet comes out at 0.750 pt per inch (true 1/8" scale). It then transforms each riser box into grid inches
  (x east of grid 7, y north of grid E).
- `takeoff.py` averages the boxes at each stack across floors. Stacks agree within 2–8.5 in floor to floor.
  Crops at every stack and floor are in [source-review/](source-review/) so the trace can be checked without
  the PDF.

## What is modeled (existing)

- **P1 garage main** 4" CW, 3" HW, 1½" HWC from the plant tie, east along the garage ceiling, then up at the
  main riser. CW in the garage is heat traced and insulated (P2.02 note).
- **R1 header** 3" CW/HW, 1¼" HWC, running north–south in the Corridor 108 ceiling, with balancing and
  isolation valves at each stack base (P3.02 symbols; valve types not reviewed).
- **Five triple stacks** A, B, C, E and F, plus a **1" CW hose-bibb riser** D:
  - Sizes step from 2"/2"/¾" to 2"/1½"/¾" to 1"/1"/½" per P3.02.
  - A, C and E offset at the R4 ceiling (P2.06 DN/UP pairs).
  - F stops at R4.
- **Branch groups:** 24 floor branch groups (stubs; the unit routing continues per P4.0x and is not traced
  here), slab penetrations at every floor, and the 1½" drop to Units 106/107 (continued in
  [highland/water](../water/README.md)).

## What is assumed

- **Pipe elevations.** No drawing gives them. Floor takeoffs sit at floor + 108 in, matching the Unit 107
  study. The garage main sits at 350.5 ft.
- **Separation.** CW/HW/HWC run at 4 in spacing.
- **Branch stubs.** 24 in long, pointing away from the corridor.
- **Existing material.** CPVC, per the owner's report; not verified.
- **Context.** The slab outlines are the grid extents, not the real slab edges.
- **Proposed design.** The PEX-A routes are offset 10 in from the existing ones; chase and ceiling space is not
  verified. Sizes are the same nominal as existing, pending engineer resizing, because PEX-A has a smaller
  bore. The 4" CW main is "material TBD", because PEX-A is not made above 3".
- **Proposed work items.** Openings (one 24 × 96 in chase opening per stack per floor, plus a 24 in corridor
  ceiling strip), firestops, riser clamps, cutover ties, new floor isolation valves and the stack order are
  illustrative.

## Flags (unresolved)

1. **Units 106/107 drop HW:** P2.03 labels 1½", P3.02 shows 1¼" (same issue date). Modeled per the plan label.

class Scene:
    def __init__(self):
        self.objects = []  # (object, phases)

    def link(self, ob, phases):
        bpy.context.scene.collection.objects.link(ob)
        self.objects.append((ob, set(phases)))
        return ob

    def box(self, name, x0, y0, z0, x1, y1, z1, mat, phases=PHASES, bevel=0.0):
        bm = bmesh.new()
        g = bmesh.ops.create_cube(bm, size=1)
        bmesh.ops.scale(bm, vec=((x1 - x0) * IN, (y1 - y0) * IN, (z1 - z0) * IN), verts=g["verts"])
        bmesh.ops.translate(bm, vec=v((x0 + x1) / 2, (y0 + y1) / 2, (z0 + z1) / 2), verts=g["verts"])
        if bevel:
            bmesh.ops.bevel(bm, geom=bm.edges[:], offset=bevel * IN, segments=2, affect="EDGES")
        me = bpy.data.meshes.new(name); bm.to_mesh(me); bm.free()
        me.materials.append(mat)
        return self.link(bpy.data.objects.new(name, me), phases)

    def tube(self, name, pts, r, mat, phases=PHASES, fillet=0.0, res=10):
        pts = rounded(pts, fillet, r) if fillet else pts
        cu = bpy.data.curves.new(name, "CURVE"); cu.dimensions = "3D"
        cu.bevel_depth = r * IN; cu.bevel_resolution = res // 2; cu.use_fill_caps = True
        sp = cu.splines.new("POLY"); sp.points.add(len(pts) - 1)
        for p, q in zip(sp.points, pts):
            p.co = (*v(*q), 1)
        cu.materials.append(mat)
        ob = self.link(bpy.data.objects.new(name, cu), phases)
        return ob

    def cyl(self, name, a, b, r, mat, phases=PHASES, seg=24):
        a, b = v(*a), v(*b); d = b - a
        bm = bmesh.new()
        g = bmesh.ops.create_cone(bm, cap_ends=True, segments=seg, radius1=r * IN, radius2=r * IN, depth=d.length)
        rot = d.normalized().to_track_quat("Z", "Y").to_matrix().to_4x4()
        bmesh.ops.transform(bm, matrix=Matrix.Translation((a + b) / 2) @ rot, verts=g["verts"])
        for f in bm.faces:
            f.smooth = True
        me = bpy.data.meshes.new(name); bm.to_mesh(me); bm.free(); me.materials.append(mat)
        return self.link(bpy.data.objects.new(name, me), phases)


def rounded(pts, R, r):
    """Replace interior corners with arcs (PEX is bent, not elbowed): bend radius R inches."""
    out = [pts[0]]
    for a, b, c in zip(pts, pts[1:], pts[2:]):
        A, B, C = Vector(a), Vector(b), Vector(c)
        u, w = (A - B), (C - B)
        if u.length < 1e-6 or w.length < 1e-6:
            continue
        ang = u.angle(w)
        if abs(ang - math.pi) < 1e-3:
            out.append(b); continue
        t = min(R / math.tan(ang / 2), u.length / 2, w.length / 2)
        p0 = B + u.normalized() * t; p1 = B + w.normalized() * t
        for k in range(9):
            s = k / 8
            out.append(tuple((1 - s) ** 2 * p0 + 2 * (1 - s) * s * B + s * s * p1))
    out.append(pts[-1])
    return out


def clip(points, x_rng, y_rng, cut=None):
    """Polyline pieces inside the bay; optionally remove a y interval (the cutover cut)."""
    def inside(p):
        return x_rng[0] <= p[0] <= x_rng[1] and y_rng[0] <= p[1] <= y_rng[1]
    pieces, cur = [], []
    for a, b in zip(points, points[1:]):
        n = max(2, int(Vector(b).__sub__(Vector(a)).length / 2))
        for k in range(n + (1 if (a, b) == tuple(zip(points, points[1:]))[-1] else 0)):
            p = tuple(a[i] + (b[i] - a[i]) * k / n for i in range(3))
            ok = inside(p) and not (cut and cut[0] < p[1] < cut[1] and abs(p[0] - HEADER_X) < 12)
            if ok:
                cur.append(p)
            elif cur:
                pieces.append(cur); cur = []
    if cur:
        pieces.append(cur)
    return [simplify(c) for c in pieces if len(c) > 1]


def simplify(pts):
    out = [pts[0]]
    for p, q in zip(pts[1:], pts[2:]):
        d1 = Vector(p) - Vector(out[-1]); d2 = Vector(q) - Vector(p)
        if d1.length and d2.length and d1.normalized().dot(d2.normalized()) > 0.9999:
            continue
        out.append(p)
    out.append(pts[-1])
    return out


def od(nominal):  # CTS outside diameter (CPVC and PEX-A share CTS OD)
    return nominal + 0.125

**Illustrative, not a contract document.** A coordination model traced from the October 2007 plumbing set, not
a survey of installed piping. Every proposed element is assumed, and none of it is engineered.

How it was built, and every source, assumption and flag: [products/risers](../../products/risers/README.md).

## Work sequence (Corridor 108 header, CPU preview)

| 5. Patch, tape, paint; remove protection | [wide](05-restore-wide.jpg) | [detail](05-restore-detail.jpg) |

![Install: new PEX-A (blue CW, red HW, white HWC) beside the existing CPVC header](03-install-detail.jpg)

These are 1280 × 720 CPU previews at 64 samples. The full-quality 4K set renders on RunPod with
`runpod_photoreal.sh`.

- **From the model:** pipe routes, sizes and the C and D branch takeoffs.
- **Illustrative:** the corridor finishes, doors, lights, hangers, protection and equipment.
- **Pending:** the finishes will be matched to site photos once they are added.

| Existing (drawing-traced) | Proposed PEX-A (grey: existing) |

- New pipe runs alongside the live system, then each stack is switched over one at a time.
